crime_highlights: Mr. Stuart then attempted to steal the sleeping man's bag.
one of Mr. Stuart's companions punched Mr. Armstrong
Mr. Stuart struck Mr. Armstrong once on the side.
Mr. Armstrong had a stab wound
The wound was around four centimetres in length, on his chest below the nipple; it was open, and required skin staples.
rationale_highlights: it is in part up to today's legal structures to respond to their effects
I must consider to what extent the factors arising from Mr. Stuart's Indigenous heritage affect his moral blameworthiness
I find there is a link between the residential school experience, the long reach of its traumatic effects and his family history which has included addiction and alcoholism
I understand Mr. Stuart's background to inform his moral blameworthiness for the offence
it does provide a mitigating factor informing his moral blameworthiness

crime_highlights: the police made a traffic stop of a van that was operating at high speeds and driving erratically
When it was pursued by the police the van did not stop.
the driver, who was later identified as Mr. Imbeault-Bachand, fled into a field
Mr. Imbeault-Bachand was driving the car that had a number of firearms
rationale_highlights: I am satisfied that the factors to be considered by the court regarding Indigenous offenders should be applied in this case
I find that Mr. Imbeault-Bachand's Indigenous status should be a factor that I consider when assessing the fitness of his sentence
note: Court only says Indigenous status is considered; no stated effect on culpability or sentence.

crime_highlights: Mr. Arnet assaulted Ms. Jack in the downtown core of Campbell River
Mr. Arnet began to shout and threaten her.
He then attacked Ms. Jack using considerable force including twisting her arm behind her back.
Ms. Jack was fearful Mr. Arnet would break her arm
it was sore and difficult for her to use for about a month
Mr. Arnet kicked Ms. Jack at least once while she was down
rationale_highlights: I must determine Mr. Arnet's moral culpability
particularly his Indigenous heritage, viewed in light of the systemic factors referred to above
the intergenerational trauma he experienced, combined with the impact of colonialism, influenced his upbringing such that he did not receive support, supervision or guidance
I conclude that Mr. Arnet's moral culpability was reduced
His moral blameworthiness is high, but it is also reduced on account of the systemic and background factors he has faced
